subject: flounder fish
title: A Flounder Is Born With an Eye on Each Side. Then One Eye Moves

scenes.text: This fish is born normal. Then one eye crawls across its head.
A flounder hatches like any fish: two to three millimetres long, swimming upright, one eye on each side.
A few days later, one eye starts forcing its way over the top of the skull. The bones bend, some almost disappear, the jaw twists.
Within a few weeks both eyes sit on one side, and the fish tips over to spend its life lying flat on the seabed.
Fossils from Italy, 45 million years old, show an ancestor caught halfway through: one eye only partly moved.
So the flounder isn't born flat. It's a normal fish that rearranged its own face.

description:
A flounder hatches as a normal, upright fish with one eye on each side; within weeks, one eye migrates over the top of its skull to join the other.
Flatfish larvae are 1.5 to 3 mm long at hatching. A few days later one eye begins to move across the head; the skull bones bend and shift, some practically disappear and re-form, and the jaws twist. Within a few weeks the fish is asymmetric and settles on its side on the seabed. Fossils about 45 million years old from Monte Bolca in Italy show primitive flatfish with the eye only halfway through its migration.
Which animal transformation beats this one?

first_comment: Bones bend, an eye slides over the skull, and the fish lies down for life. Caterpillar to butterfly, or this: which is the weirder makeover?
